key_insight: MM-WebAgent uses a hierarchical multimodal agent framework to coordinate global planning and local AIGC modules, producing webpages that are stylistically consistent and globally coherent instead of assembled from isolated elements.
problem_solved: Solves style inconsistency and poor global coherence in automated webpage generation when integrating image/text/video AIGC tools, which typically produce disjointed elements that don't form a unified UI/UX.
method: Hierarchical agent architecture: a global planner sets page-level layout, style, and constraints while local agents generate components guided by that plan.
Multimodal coordination: integrate image, text, and layout generators under shared style and content constraints to ensure cross-modal consistency.
Iterative refinement & constraint enforcement: feedback loops align local outputs to the global plan, correcting mismatches and improving coherence.
impact: Makes AI-driven webpage generation practical at scale by reducing manual editing and delivering coherent, on-brand designs; valuable for teams building automated site builders, design systems, and AIGC-powered UX tools.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram showing global planner, local multimodal agents, and feedback loop
Side-by-side before/after webpage examples illustrating inconsistency vs. coherent design
Pipeline flowchart: input prompt → global plan → multimodal generators → refinement
Style-consistency visualization (palette mapping or heatmap across components)
paper_title: MM-WebAgent: A Hierarchical Multimodal Web Agent for Webpage Generation
paper_authors: Yan Li, Zezi Zeng, Yifan Yang, Yuqing Yang, Ning Liao
